metadata.title: Likelihood-Ranked Synthetic Selection in Self-Consuming Diffusion: Minority Extinction Ordering at Moderate Imbalance
metadata.description:
Self-consuming training loops can induce model collapse. We study unlabeled likelihood ranking of synthetic samples in self-consuming DDPM training, emphasizing moderate imbalance. Define the minority-mass ratio r = m(1)/m(0). Results are stratified by imbalance ρ. At ρ=5 (n=5), bottom-k > random-k > top-k on all seeds with large paired effects (Cohen dz ≈ −1.96 / +1.65); reported as directional because exact Wilcoxon p=0.0625 is the discrete minimum at n=5 and cannot reach p<0.05. At ρ=10 (n=3), the order fails (0/3) and contrasts are near null (minority-mass floor). Strongest powered claim: top-k does not improve sliced W2 at generation 1 (ΔW2>0 on 8/8 cells; exact p=0.0078; Holm-adjusted p=0.039). Directional transfers (8D GMM, Digits-PCA; n=3) match ρ=5; Digits-CVAE was inconclusive.

Code: https://github.com/muhammadalamzeb/likelihood-rank-self-consuming-diffusion
metadata.notes: Empirical short preprint / workshop-scope note. Retention at rho=5 is directional (exact Wilcoxon floored at n=5); primary powered claim is W2 at generation 1. Stratified by imbalance rho.
